<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518913940_theRebbe_399" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518913940_theRebbe_399__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The Baal Shem Tov's interpretation of the verse "Blow the shofar in the month" teaches that one's service must always be with renewal, not as a fixed habit.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And behold, there is a known precise point of our teacher the Baal Shem Tov</t>
    <t s="1">(in Kesser Shem Tov6)</t>
    <t s="2">regarding this verse,</t>
    <t s="3">that it should have said "Blow a shofar in the month."</t>
    <t s="4">And the Baal Shem Tov explained this,</t>
    <t s="5">that a person should constantly see that he be "in the month" — meaning to renew good deeds, that it should not be like a fixed routine.</t>
    <t s="6">And one can explain the matter,</t>
    <t s="7">that since this verse speaks about a fundamental and general matter,</t>
    <t s="8">the matter of Rosh HaShanah and the matter of "Make Me king over you,"</t>
    <t s="9">therefore it contains a fundamental and general instruction in the general service of each and every Jew,</t>
    <t s="10">that the service must be in a manner of renewal,</t>
    <t s="11">that at every time and every moment and in every single thing he does,</t>
    <t s="12">he should do it as something truly new7.</t>
    <t s="13">[And perhaps one can add to this further,</t>
    <t s="14">that this is also the precise meaning of the word "Tik'u" (blow),</t>
    <t s="15">"Tik'u" also from the term strength and might8,</t>
    <t s="16">that he should embed himself with the greatest strength and might without any changes in his service,</t>
    <t s="17">until he embeds himself in an eternal manner,</t>
    <t s="18">so that through this every moment of his service is a new thing].</t>
    <t s="19">And with this one can explain the connection to what was said previously in the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov there,</t>
    <t s="20">that the matter of a miracle is that the thing was renewed for the first time, and when it comes repeatedly it is called nature — meaning that in truth everything is a miracle.</t>
    <t s="21">And one can connect this with the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov9</t>
    <t s="22">that every thing in the world is renewed at every moment,</t>
    <t s="23">and what is called by the name "nature" is only because the renewal already occurred previously</t>
    <t s="24">(and was not renewed now for the first time).</t>
    <t s="25">And through contemplation on this very matter — that in truth everything is a miracle and a new thing — this gives power to every matter in service, that he should do it in a manner of something truly new.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The term "Keseh" means a fixed time and season, and on Rosh HaShanah the renewal of time and space is completed through the creation of Adam.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it continues afterward in the maamar</t>
    <t s="1">(of 5707)</t>
    <t s="2">there,</t>
    <t s="3">that the explanation of "Keseh" is</t>
    <t s="4">(also)</t>
    <t s="5">a term for time and season10,</t>
    <t s="6">that there is a limited time and season to draw down the aspect of Malchus.</t>
    <t s="7">And one must explain the connection of this matter</t>
    <t s="8">("Keseh" as a term for time and season)</t>
    <t s="9">to the matter of Rosh HaShanah,</t>
    <t s="10">based on the well-known teaching of the Maggid</t>
    <t s="11">[which is brought in the discourse of the Alter Rebbe printed in the Siddur with Chassidus11</t>
    <t s="12">that was written by his son and successor, the Mitteler Rebbe],</t>
    <t s="13">that time is created.</t>
    <t s="14">And from this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="15">that just as on Rosh HaShanah a renewal is effected in the creation of the entire world,</t>
    <t s="16">as the statement12</t>
    <t s="17">"This day is the beginning of Your works, a remembrance of the first day,"</t>
    <t s="18">so too, on Rosh HaShanah there is the renewal of the entire creation of the boundaries of time and place and their existence</t>
    <t s="19">(for time and place are boundaries of the world13).</t>
    <t s="20">And the matter is,</t>
    <t s="21">that behold, there is a known precise point</t>
    <t s="22">(in Likkutei Torah14</t>
    <t s="23">etc.),</t>
    <t s="24">that on the 25th of Elul the world was created15,</t>
    <t s="25">and on Rosh HaShanah it is the sixth day of Creation,</t>
    <t s="26">the day of the creation of Adam, the first man,</t>
    <t s="27">and what is this "This day is the beginning of Your works, a remembrance of the first day"?</t>
    <t s="28">And it is explained in this14,</t>
    <t s="29">that although the creation of the entire world was in the first moment of the six days of Creation,</t>
    <t s="30">as it is written16</t>
    <t s="31">"In the beginning, G-d created the heavens and the earth,"</t>
    <t s="32">and all the more so that then the boundaries of time and place and their existence were created</t>
    <t s="33">(for they are boundaries of the world as above),</t>
    <t s="34">nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="35">the perfection of creation was specifically on the sixth day of Creation,</t>
    <t s="36">the day of the creation of Adam.</t>
    <t s="37">Therefore specifically this day is called "the beginning of Your works and a remembrance of the first day."</t>
    <t s="38">And with this one will also understand that this day is called by the name "Keseh" simply,</t>
    <t s="39">which is a time and season,</t>
    <t s="40">for although the coming into being of the boundaries of time and place and their existence was in the first moment,</t>
    <t s="41">nevertheless, specifically on this day is the perfection of the coming into being of the boundary and existence of time</t>
    <t s="42">(and place),</t>
    <t s="43">because this is the day of the creation of Adam, the first man.</t>
    <t s="44">For Adam, the first man, effected perfection in all of creation through drawing down G-dliness</t>
    <t s="45">(His kingship)</t>
    <t s="46">into creation17,</t>
    <t s="47">for this is what is called "Adam" from the term "I will be like the Most High"18,</t>
    <t s="48">that he drew down His G-dliness below to make for Him a dwelling place in the lower realms within the boundaries of time and place.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Just as Adam perfected creation, so too every Jew each year draws down G-dliness, and Adam was created alone to teach that each Jewish soul is a whole world.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And behold, just as it was the first time,</t>
    <t s="1">that Adam, the first man, then effected perfection in all of creation,</t>
    <t s="2">including in the matter of time,</t>
    <t s="3">so too it is every single year through the service of each and every Jew,</t>
    <t s="4">who is also called "Adam" from the term "I will be like the Most High"19,</t>
    <t s="5">meaning that each and every Jew through his service draws down His G-dliness below.</t>
    <t s="6">And on the contrary,</t>
    <t s="7">therefore man was created alone, to teach you that whoever sustains a single soul of Israel, it is as if he sustained an entire world20,</t>
    <t s="8">meaning that this that Adam, the first man, was created alone,</t>
    <t s="9">"I will be like the Unique One of the world"</t>
    <t s="10">(the aspect of Yechidah, which is above the aspect of Echad21),</t>
    <t s="11">because of a single soul of Israel.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
